title: When Do Induction Heads Fail? Boundary Conditions for the Induction Circuit

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with a gap: mapping induction head failure conditions calibrates trust in circuit descriptions but the direct safety relevance is limited compared to other ideas.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TransformerLens tutorials cover induction heads directly. Constructing [A][B]...[A][?] test sequences and measuring probability boosts is accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: systematic parameter sweep (distance, frequency, pattern length) on one model with one well-defined metric (probability boost). Clear deliverable.

novelty.reasoning: The architectural constraints and emergence dynamics of induction heads have been studied (arXiv 2404.07129), and selective induction heads introduce new variants (ICLR 2025). However, the specific systematic parameter sweep of boundary conditions (distance, frequency, pattern length) for standard induction heads has not been fully addressed. The idea is partially novel in its empirical focus on behavioral failure boundaries.

evidence.source: What needs to go right for an induction head? (arXiv 2404.07129, 2024)
evidence.finding: Systematically studies architectural constraints for induction heads, showing one-layer transformers cannot solve the task unless size is linear in sequence length, and analyzing subcircuit requirements.
Identifies selective induction heads that differ from traditional ones, where the circuit selectively copies tokens based on semantic comparison rather than purely positional matching.

evidence.source: In-context Learning and Induction Heads (Transformer Circuits, 2022)
evidence.finding: Foundational work documenting induction head mechanics, including emergence dynamics and diversity of induction heads, but noting limited understanding of failure conditions.
